messages:
elaine: heads-up — i'm sketching a proposal for runtime credential strata. idea is we normalize a few incoming credential types at the gateway into a canonical actor envelope so downstream services only need one auth surface. @kai @sam any immediate red flags? :thinking_face:

kai: sounds promising. main worry is token introspection cost at high qps. need caching or an async warm-up path.

sam: agree on cache. also think we should keep 3 explicit strata: 1) customer edge API keys (long-lived, per-project), 2) service-issued project tokens (rotating), 3) operator/infra ephemeral creds (short, HSM-backed). mapping to actor + scope feels right.

elaine: exactly. proposal sketch: gateway extracts and normalizes into header pair ``x-rw-actor`` + ``x-rw-scope``. then policy gate runs against actor+scope. caching TTL default 5m with invalidation on revoke. quick proto config: 
```
# gateway mapping
authorization: Bearer <token>
-> x-rw-actor: actor:svc-123
-> x-rw-scope: project:pj-456
```

jordan: how do we handle API keys that embed project vs org scoping? some customers expect org-wide keys.

sam: canonicalize scope with precedence: explicit token scope > key-attribute > org-default. put a strict flag in token metadata to prevent accidental upscoping.

kai: for introspection: avoid blocking request path on remote calls. flow: lookup cache -> if miss, return provisional decision based on token type (low-trust) + enqueue introspect -> once introspect finishes, upgrade or mark audit. we'd need clear SLOs for provisional behavior.

elaine: love the provisional idea. need to be careful with sensitive operations (billing, admin). those should require confirmed introspection. we can tag routes as "high-assurance" in route config.

sam: operator creds: require short TTL + KMS/HSM signer verification, no caching beyond 30s. also revoke path should be immediate via push invalidation to gateway kv.

jordan: what about RBAC mapping complexity? if gateway provides actor+scope only, services still need role lookup. do we centralize role resolution too?

kai: two options: 1) gateway resolves roles into a compact set of role claims and passes them (fast, smaller call surface); 2) services perform role evaluation by calling auth service. tradeoff: duplication of logic vs network roundtrips.

elaine: preference is hybrid: gateway resolves common roles (read/write/owner) for perf-critical paths, services can call full policy engine for complex decisions. keep token envelope small (list of role ids, expiration, and signature).

sam: one more: audit and trace. every normalization event should append a structured audit entry with token_id, resolved_actor, scope, and source. wire that into tracing with a trace-id.

auth-bot: FYI — brief run: token-introspect endpoint currently avg 28ms p95 45ms, cache hit reduces to ~1ms. Logging spike on revokes currently has 3s propagation on push invalidation.

elaine: ok next steps: I'll draft an RFC with: canonical envelope spec, cache invalidation design, provisional decision model, route high-assurance flag, and rollout checklist. plan a 30m sync next Tue. thanks all. :thumbsup:
